name: github
description: Read and open issues, comments and pull requests in GitHub repositories, signed in with your own GitHub App.

tools.name: list_repositories
tools.description: List the repositories the agent's access names, with whether each is private and when it last changed. Reads only.

tools.name: get_repository
tools.description: Read a repository's details: description, default branch, visibility, address. Reads only.

tools.name: list_issues
tools.description: List a repository's issues by state, labels or search words, at most 50. Reads only.

tools.name: get_issue
tools.description: Read one issue with its body and latest 20 comments. Reads only.

tools.name: create_issue
tools.description: Open an issue in a repository, when the agent's access allows creating and commenting. Creates an issue as the account you signed in with.

tools.name: comment
tools.description: Comment on an issue or pull request, when the agent's access allows creating and commenting. Posts a comment as the account you signed in with.

tools.name: list_pull_requests
tools.description: List a repository's pull requests by state or base branch, at most 50. Reads only.

tools.name: get_pull_request
tools.description: Read one pull request, and its diff when asked. Reads only.

tools.name: create_pull_request
tools.description: Open a pull request from a branch already on GitHub, when the agent's access allows creating and commenting. Creates a pull request as the account you signed in with; moves no commits.

tools.name: list_branches
tools.description: List a repository's branches and the commit each points at. Reads only.

tools.name: compare
tools.description: Compare two branches, tags or commits: commits ahead and behind, files changed. Reads only.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Name the GitHub account the connection signs in as, for Test connection. Reads only.

repositories.title: Repositories
repositories.description: Each one owner/name, such as acme/widgets, or a pattern such as acme/*, which covers every repository directly under acme. * is the only wildcard. Capitals do not matter.

write.title: May create and comment
write.description: Lets the agent open issues and pull requests and comment on them in those repositories, as the account you signed in with.

kivali.setup_notes:
Agents reach GitHub through a GitHub App you register yourself. It takes a few minutes, once.

1. On GitHub, open the settings of the account or organization that owns the repositories agents should reach: **Settings**, **Developer settings**, **GitHub Apps**, then **New GitHub App**.
2. Give it a name, such as "Kivali agents". GitHub App names are unique across GitHub.
3. For **Homepage URL**, enter any address, such as your company's website.
4. For **Callback URL**, paste the redirect address shown above this form, `{{redirect_url}}`. In Kivali Desktop it is a 127.0.0.1 address, and GitHub accepts it with any port.
5. Leave **Request user authorization (OAuth) during installation** off.
6. Tick **Enable Device Flow**.
7. Under **Webhook**, untick **Active**.
8. Under **Permissions**, **Repository permissions**, set **Contents** to Read-only, **Issues** to Read and write, **Metadata** to Read-only and **Pull requests** to Read and write. Leave the rest at No access.
9. Under **Where can this GitHub App be installed?**, choose **Only on this account**.
10. Choose **Create GitHub App**.
11. Copy the **Client ID** into **Client id** below.
12. Choose **Generate a new client secret** and paste it into **Client secret** below. GitHub shows it once.
13. Under **Optional features**, leave **Expire user authorization tokens** on, so Kivali can renew the sign-in.
14. In the app's settings, choose **Install App** and install it on that account or organization, for the repositories agents should reach. Agents reach only repositories the app is installed on, and only those their access names.

Then choose **Save connection**, and **Sign in with a code** or **Sign in in your browser**.
